narrativeBlocks.title: The scene
narrativeBlocks.body: To free Thebes from plague, Oedipus seeks Laius’ killer and curses the unknown culprit. The investigation eventually identifies Oedipus himself. The skill and determination used to protect the city turn back upon its ruler.

narrativeBlocks.title: What the source does
narrativeBlocks.body: Source quotation (translation; whitespace normalized): “as their champion I maintain the cause Both of the god and of the murdered King. And on the murderer this curse I lay (On him and all the partners in his guilt):— Wretch, may he pine in utter wretchedness! And for myself, if with my privity He gain admittance to my hearth, I pray The curse I laid on”

narrativeBlocks.title: Why it matters
narrativeBlocks.body: Interpretation: His intelligence is genuinely heroic, but it leads to recognition rather than rescue; knowledge can be necessary and devastating.

narrativeBlocks.title: Read it carefully
narrativeBlocks.body: Watch how the proclamation changes meaning as the inquiry proceeds. Oedipus speaks against an unknown culprit, while the audience can recognise that his investigation will expose the speaker himself.

narrativeBlocks.title: Carry it forward
narrativeBlocks.body: This is heroic problem-solving turned into reversal.

quiz.explanation: The killing of Laius. Revisit the named passage and distinguish its narrative from the lesson’s interpretation.

quiz.prompt: What gives his curse dramatic irony?

choices.text: The audience knows Laius is still ruling Thebes.
Creon has already confessed to the killing.
The unknown killer he condemns will prove to be himself.
